title: Feather River College Volleyball Players Chloe Albiez and Teya Gibbs Named All-Americans - NewsBreak
text:
59 minutes ago The California Community College Women's Volleyball Association (CCCWVCA) has announced its 2025 All-State, All-Region, and All-American selections. The announcement was made on Wednesday. Several athletes were recognized, including sophomores Chloe Albiez and Teya Gibbs from Feather River College. Both received All-American honors for their performance this season.
Chloe Albiez, an outside hitter for Feather River, was named a First Team All-American. Albiez was also the MVP of last year's 3C2A State Championships. She finished the regular season ranked fourth in overall kills with 424 and points with 495.5.
Teya Gibbs, also from Feather River, was named a Third Team All-American. Gibbs, a setter, led the state in assists with 1,137 during the season. Her play contributed to Feather River's results on the court.
Other honorees include Clairie Thomas from Desert College, who led the state in kills and points, and Hadlee Gray from San Joaquin Delta, who ranked second in those categories. The awards also introduced a new Libero of the Year honor. Mayah Tiscareno of Mt. San Antonio and Allison Wood of Sequoias received this recognition.
Coaching awards were also given. Chuck Cutenese of Orange Coast was named South Region Coach of the Year after an undefeated regular season. Molly Hummel of San Joaquin Delta was named North Region Coach of the Year for leading her team to a 27-1 record and a Big 8 title. The 2025 CCCWVCA awards recognize achievements in California community college women's volleyball.
